02 / 24. The goal
The target

135,000 organic trials in 2026. Here's how we get there.

The number
~135K
organic trials · full-year 2026 · +27–29% YoY
Why this number

Organic is the lowest-CAC growth lever we have. Paid CAC is rising 17–110% across every channel. Every organic trial we add compounds. It does not decay with spend.

135K is achievable and not the ceiling. If the 9.72% signup-to-trial rate holds structural, the floor moves to ~140K.

Two problems this plan attacks
01
Acquisition
The channel is growing but not converting efficiently. 373K blog sessions delivering under 0.1% of trials. The plan builds a second acquisition engine that doesn't depend on a single page.
02
Retention
17.6% monthly churn. 1 in 5 exits is personalization-addressable. Acquisition compounds only when the bucket stops leaking. The Plait layer addresses this directly.
→
The $47M opportunity
Each percentage point of monthly churn reduction equals $47.2M in steady-state ARR. The acquisition plan funds itself. The retention play is the compounding prize.

06 / 24. How growth happens
Point of view

Organic growth in this channel happens through two unlocks we haven't fully built.

01
A second acquisition surface that converts high-intent traffic we already have.

~450K blog sessions and 208K meal-planning intent sessions per quarter convert at near zero today. The surface to capture them doesn't exist. We build it. Acquisition compounds.

This is what we haven't focused on: a standalone decision surface that earns the subscriber before they ever see CookUnity.

02
Preference data captured at acquisition, so the subscriber stays.

17.6% monthly churn. One in five exits is preventable with personalization. We don't capture goal, dietary needs, or cooking tolerance at acquisition today. That data, captured on day zero, is worth $47M ARR per percentage point of churn it prevents.

Acquisition compounds only when retention holds. Both unlocks work together or neither works at scale.

Plait · Category thesis
18 / 24. The insight
Separate from the plan · personal thesis
Category thesis

"People don't want better food options.
They want fewer decisions."

Every category-defining platform of the last fifteen years removed a decision. it did not expand a choice set. That is the pattern. That is the opening.

UberDid not add more transportation options.Removed the transportation decision.
SpotifyDid not add more music.Removed the music decision.
NetflixDid not add more content.Removed the content decision.

Factor, HelloFresh, Freshly, Mob. Every competitor still asks the user to choose meals. Plait removes the decision. That is the opening.
